The measured Part B allowed amount works out at $145.86 per mcg, 86.7% of WAC, which is the usual relation between a Medicare allowed amount and a list price

column11: a capped course finished inside one beneficiary-year, so no patient carries forward. The label caps every regimen: the MRD-positive course is 1 induction cycle plus up to 3 consolidation cycles, each 28 days of continuous infusion followed by a 14-day treatment-free interval, 168 days in total (BLINCYTO prescribing information, section 2.1, openFDA drug/label). Measured on the same beneficiaries the price is quoted on: CMS Part B 2024 (drug_demand) is 591,152 dosage units over 357 beneficiaries = 1,656 mcg each, and a 28-day cycle at the fixed 28 mcg/day dose is 784 mcg, so a Medicare beneficiary averages 2.11 cycles in a year. Kantarjian H et al., N Engl J Med 2017;376:836-847, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1609783 (TOWER, 405 adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL given blinatumomab): the median number of treatment cycles was 2, range 1 to 9. The published median course and the measured annual consumption are the same 2 cycles, so the course sits inside the year
column12: At 1.0 the engine's revenue is each year's new patients times the per-beneficiary price, which is how the book already treats a capped course on Roche's cevostamab and Regeneron's odronextamab. The case against: the relapsed or refractory regimen runs to 2 induction plus 3 consolidation 42-day cycles and up to 4 continued-therapy 84-day cycles, 546 days if a patient takes all nine, so the tail of the distribution does bill into a second year. The measured 2.11 cycles a beneficiary-year says that tail is small; the figure that would replace this is a CMS patient-level episode length, which the public files do not carry

column11: the approved disease. BLINCYTO is indicated for CD19-positive B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia in adult and pediatric patients one month and older, in three settings: MRD at or above 0.1% in first or second complete remission, relapsed or refractory disease, and the consolidation phase of multiphase chemotherapy in Philadelphia chromosome-negative disease (current label, openFDA drug/label, last_updated 2026-10-26). Both studies behind this unit enrol inside it: NCT04521231 is subcutaneous blinatumomab in relapsed or refractory and MRD-positive B-cell precursor ALL, 181 participants; NCT07223190 compares subcutaneous against intravenous blinatumomab in newly diagnosed adult B-cell precursor ALL, 560 participants
column12: a route change, not a new population. The $1,559mm FY2025 revenue already contains these patients, so no pool is seeded and nothing is added. The subcutaneous form can still matter to price per patient, to the sites that can treat, and to the life of the franchise past the intravenous presentation; none of those is a patient pool and none is priced here
